newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber untraded a day after baht plunge.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber untraded a day after baht plunge.

text.p: Singapore rubber futures were untraded in Thursday's morning session and were indicated at narrowly mixed levels after plunging yesterday on the sharp fall in the Thai baht on the currency's flotation, brokers said.

"There is nothing to report today. Prices in Tokyo have stabilised a little bit but we haven't seen any follow-through buying here. We are just waiting to see what happens in the afternoon," a local broker said.
"There's really no activity today because we are waiting for a clearer view of the Thai baht float," another broker said.
At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 92.75 U.S. cents a kg compared with Wednesday's settlement of 94.75.
September RSS1 was indicated at 136.50 Singapore cents (95 U.S. cents) a kg against Wednesday's 137.75 cents.
September TSR20 was indicated at 133.50 Singapore cents (93 U.S. cents) a kg from 131.75 cents.
